projects.title: Techcon GH LLC – Infrastructure Deployment
projects.description: Review the project requirements, build the environment on your own system, and use each section as the technical specification for the deployment.

sections.title: Instructions
sections.summary: This project is requirement-driven. You are expected to determine the implementation method, build order, and validation approach on your own system.

blocks.title: How to Use This Project
items: Read the active section carefully before making configuration decisions.
Use the requirements as the build specification for your environment.
Return to the relevant section whenever you need to confirm naming, counts, limits, or service expectations.
Mark a section reviewed only after you are satisfied that your environment reflects that section's requirements.

blocks.title: Design Standard
items: This project gives exact specifications, but it does not provide procedural steps.
You are responsible for selecting the tools, management consoles, commands, and workflow needed to complete the build.
The goal is not only to produce a working environment, but to demonstrate that you can translate requirements into implementation.

blocks.title: General Build Expectations
items: Use consistent naming across servers, client systems, users, groups, folders, and shares.
Keep service placement aligned to the server role assignments defined in this project.
Validate the environment as you build so that earlier design decisions do not create downstream issues.
Treat every section as part of one connected environment rather than as isolated configuration tasks.

sections.title: Scenario
sections.summary: This section introduces the organization, the operating environment, and the overall mission of the project.

blocks.title: Organization Overview
blocks.content: Techcon GH LLC is a growing technology consulting firm establishing a structured Windows Server environment for its New York office. The organization needs centralized identity management, dependable network services, controlled access to shared data, and a consistent desktop experience for staff across its major departments.

blocks.title: Project Objective
blocks.content: Your task is to build the first production-style infrastructure for the office based on the requirements in this project. The completed environment must support directory services, address management, file services, security policy enforcement, and client integration in a way that is organized, scalable, and easy to administer.

sections.title: Server Configuration Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the server inventory, addressing, role placement, and storage expectations for the environment.

rows.label: TC-DC1
rows.value: 172.16.1.10 — Active Directory Domain Services, DNS, DHCP

rows.label: TC-DC2
rows.value: 172.16.1.11 — Active Directory Domain Services, DNS, File Services, Storage Replica

blocks.title: General Server Requirements
items: Both servers must use static IPv4 addressing.
Both servers must be named correctly before server roles are installed.
Both servers must be able to communicate with each other across the network.
Server role placement must follow the assignments defined in this project.

rows.label: TC-DC1 Data Volume
rows.value: One additional 50 GB data disk to support replicated shared data requirements.

rows.label: TC-DC2 Data Volume
rows.value: One additional 50 GB data disk to host departmental shares, home directories, and replicated storage.

sections.title: Active Directory Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the forest, domain controller placement, FSMO role handling, directory hierarchy, and principal object requirements.

blocks.title: Forest and Domain Controller Requirements
items: Create a new forest named techcongh.local.
Promote TC-DC1 as the first Domain Controller in the forest.
Promote TC-DC2 as an additional Domain Controller in the same domain.
Active Directory replication must be operational between both Domain Controllers.
The final environment must support normal authentication and directory operations after both promotions are complete.

blocks.title: FSMO Requirements
items: Identify all five FSMO roles in the environment.
Transfer the PDC Emulator role to TC-DC2.
Transfer the RID Master role to TC-DC2.
Document the final FSMO role placement as part of the completed environment review.

blocks.title: OU Structure
blocks.content:
TechconGH
│
├── Sales-Dep
│   ├── Sales-Users
│   ├── Sales-Groups
│   └── Sales-PCs
│
├── Marketing-Dep
│   ├── Marketing-Users
│   ├── Marketing-Groups
│   └── Marketing-PCs
│
├── Operations-Dep
│   ├── Operations-Users
│   ├── Operations-Groups
│   └── Operations-PCs
│
├── HR-Dep
│   ├── HR-Users
│   ├── HR-Groups
│   └── HR-PCs
│
└── IT-Admins

blocks.title: Naming Standards
items: User accounts must follow the firstname.lastname naming format.
Department groups must follow the <Department>-<Function> format.
Client computer accounts must follow the TC-CL naming pattern.
Permissions must be assigned using groups rather than direct user assignments.

sections.title: Network Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the addressing model, DNS requirements, DHCP scope design, and client lease behavior for the office network.

blocks.title: DNS Requirements
items: Install DNS on both Domain Controllers.
Use an Active Directory-integrated DNS zone for techcongh.local.
DNS data must replicate between both Domain Controllers.
The environment must support internal name resolution for servers and domain resources.

blocks.title: Addressing and Lease Behavior
items: Server IP addresses must not be assigned through DHCP.
The client system TC-CL1 must always receive the same IP address from DHCP.
That consistent address assignment must be implemented through DHCP rather than through static addressing on the client.
The network must support normal client lease issuance, renewal, and DNS registration behavior.

sections.title: File and Storage Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the storage layout, departmental shares, home directory model, FSRM controls, and replication requirements for shared data.

blocks.title: Folder Structure on TC-DC2
blocks.content:
D:\Shares\
│
├── Sales
├── Marketing
├── Operations
├── HR
│
└── Home
    ├── <one folder per user>

blocks.title: Access Model
items: Create one departmental folder for each department listed in the scenario.
Create one home folder for each user under D:\Shares\Home.
Use group-based access assignments rather than direct user permissions.
Implement share permissions and NTFS permissions in a way that supports departmental access control.

blocks.title: Storage Replica Requirement
items: Configure storage replication between TC-DC1 and TC-DC2.
The replicated data set must cover the shared data structure hosted under D:\Shares.
The final environment must support synchronized shared data across the two servers.

sections.title: GPO Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the policy design, security settings, user restrictions, mapped drives, and folder redirection standards for the environment.

blocks.title: GPO Design Standards
items: GPOs must be clearly named and linked at appropriate levels.
Policies must not be linked at the domain root unless the scope requires domain-level application.
User and computer settings must be targeted in a way that aligns with the OU structure.
The IT-Admins OU must not receive the workstation restrictions or standard user environment controls defined in this project.

blocks.title: Audit Policy Requirements
items: Audit Logon/Logoff — Success and Failure
Audit Account Logon — Success and Failure
Audit Object Access — Success
Audit Policy Change — Success
Audit Account Management — Success

blocks.title: User Environment and Restriction Policies
items: Disable Control Panel.
Disable PC Settings.
Prevent access to Command Prompt.
Prevent access to Registry Editor.
Configure a standard company wallpaper.
Prevent users from changing the wallpaper.

blocks.title: Folder Redirection and Session Security
items: Redirect Desktop to \\TC-DC2\Home\%USERNAME%.
Redirect Documents to \\TC-DC2\Home\%USERNAME%.
Enforce a screen lock after 10 minutes of inactivity.
Require a password when the workstation resumes from the lock screen.
Disable access to removable storage devices.

sections.title: Client Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the endpoint configuration and the expected user experience after the server-side build is complete.

rows.label: IP Assignment
rows.value: DHCP with a consistent reserved address

blocks.title: Client Integration Requirements
items: Join the client system to the techcongh.local domain.
Place the client computer account in the appropriate departmental Computers OU.
Log on to the client using a user account from the HR department.
The client must receive the correct policies, mapped drives, and redirected folders after sign-in.

blocks.title: Expected Client Experience
items: The client receives its address information from DHCP.
The client resolves internal resources through the domain DNS infrastructure.
The user can access the correct departmental resources based on group membership.
The user environment reflects the restrictions and standardization settings defined in Group Policy.

sections.title: Final Review
sections.summary: Use this section as your closeout check before you consider the project finished.

blocks.title: Environment Review Checklist
items: The domain and both Domain Controllers are functioning correctly.
DNS and DHCP support normal client connectivity and name resolution.
The directory structure, users, groups, and client placement match the project specification.
Departmental shares, home folders, quotas, file screening, and storage replication are configured as required.
Group Policy settings apply to the intended users and systems without affecting the IT-Admins OU.
The client system integrates successfully into the environment and reflects the expected user experience.
